1: package llmverify
2: import chisel3._
3: import chisel3.util._
4: import chisel3.ltl._
5: import chisel3.ltl.Sequence._
6: 
7: // Define enums using ChiselEnum
8: object Selection extends ChiselEnum {
9:   val A, B, C, X = Value
10: }
11: 
12: object ControllerState extends ChiselEnum {
13:   val IDLE, READY, BUSY = Value
14: }
15: 
16: object ClientState extends ChiselEnum {
17:   val NO_REQ, REQ, HAVE_TOKEN = Value
18: }
19: 
20: // Controller module
21: class Controller extends Module {
22:   val io = IO(new Bundle {
23:     val req = Input(Bool())
24:     val sel = Input(Selection())
25:     val id = Input(Selection())
26:     val ack = Output(Bool())
27:     val pass_token = Output(Bool())
28:   })
29:   
30:   val state = RegInit(ControllerState.IDLE)
31:   val ackReg = RegInit(false.B)
32:   val passTokenReg = RegInit(true.B)
33:   
34:   val isSelected = (io.sel === io.id)
35:   
36:   io.ack := ackReg
37:   io.pass_token := passTokenReg
38:   
39:   switch(state) {
40:     is(ControllerState.IDLE) {
41:       when(isSelected) {
42:         when(io.req) {
43:           state := ControllerState.READY
44:           passTokenReg := false.B
45:         }.otherwise {
46:           passTokenReg := true.B
47:         }
48:       }.otherwise {
49:         passTokenReg := false.B
50:       }
51:     }
52:     is(ControllerState.READY) {
53:       state := ControllerState.BUSY
54:       ackReg := true.B
55:     }
56:     is(ControllerState.BUSY) {
57:       when(!io.req) {
58:         state := ControllerState.IDLE
59:         ackReg := false.B
60:         passTokenReg := true.B
61:       }
62:     }
63:   }
64: }
65: 
66: // Arbiter module
67: class Arbiter extends Module {
68:   val io = IO(new Bundle {
69:     val active = Input(Bool())
70:     val sel = Output(Selection())
71:   })
72:   
73:   val state = RegInit(Selection.A)
74:   
75:   io.sel := Mux(io.active, state, Selection.X)
76:   
77:   when(io.active) {
78:     switch(state) {
79:       is(Selection.A) {
80:         state := Selection.B
81:       }
82:       is(Selection.B) {
83:         state := Selection.C
84:       }
85:       is(Selection.C) {
86:         state := Selection.A
87:       }
88:     }
89:   }
90: }
91: 
92: // Client module
93: class Client extends Module {
94:   val io = IO(new Bundle {
95:     val ack = Input(Bool())
96:     val req = Output(Bool())
97:   })
98:   
99:   val state = RegInit(ClientState.NO_REQ)
100:   val reqReg = RegInit(false.B)
101:   
102:   // Simple pseudo-random choice using LFSR
103:   val lfsr = RegInit(1.U(8.W))
104:   val randChoice = lfsr(0)
105:   lfsr := Cat(lfsr(6), lfsr(5), lfsr(4), lfsr(3), lfsr(2), lfsr(1), lfsr(0), lfsr(6) ^ lfsr(5))
106:   
107:   io.req := reqReg
108:   
109:   switch(state) {
110:     is(ClientState.NO_REQ) {
111:       when(randChoice) {
112:         reqReg := true.B
113:         state := ClientState.REQ
114:       }
115:     }
116:     is(ClientState.REQ) {
117:       when(io.ack) {
118:         state := ClientState.HAVE_TOKEN
119:       }
120:     }
121:     is(ClientState.HAVE_TOKEN) {
122:       when(randChoice) {
123:         reqReg := false.B
124:         state := ClientState.NO_REQ
125:       }
126:     }
127:   }
128: }
129: 
130: // Main module
131: class Main extends Module {
132:   val io = IO(new Bundle {
133:     val ackA = Output(Bool())
134:     val ackB = Output(Bool())
135:     val ackC = Output(Bool())
136:     // Additional outputs to preserve internal signals
137:     val sel = Output(Selection())
138:     val active = Output(Bool())
139:     val reqA = Output(Bool())
140:     val reqB = Output(Bool())
141:     val reqC = Output(Bool())
142:     val pass_tokenA = Output(Bool())
143:     val pass_tokenB = Output(Bool())
144:     val pass_tokenC = Output(Bool())
145:   })
146:   
147:   // Instantiate controllers
148:   val controllerA = Module(new Controller)
149:   val controllerB = Module(new Controller)
150:   val controllerC = Module(new Controller)
151:   
152:   // Instantiate arbiter
153:   val arbiter = Module(new Arbiter)
154:   
155:   // Instantiate clients
156:   val clientA = Module(new Client)
157:   val clientB = Module(new Client)
158:   val clientC = Module(new Client)
159:   
160:   // Connect controllers
161:   controllerA.io.req := clientA.io.req
162:   controllerA.io.sel := arbiter.io.sel
163:   controllerA.io.id := Selection.A
164:   
165:   controllerB.io.req := clientB.io.req
166:   controllerB.io.sel := arbiter.io.sel
167:   controllerB.io.id := Selection.B
168:   
169:   controllerC.io.req := clientC.io.req
170:   controllerC.io.sel := arbiter.io.sel
171:   controllerC.io.id := Selection.C
172:   
173:   // Connect clients
174:   clientA.io.ack := controllerA.io.ack
175:   clientB.io.ack := controllerB.io.ack
176:   clientC.io.ack := controllerC.io.ack
177:   
178:   // Connect arbiter
179:   val active = controllerA.io.pass_token || controllerB.io.pass_token || controllerC.io.pass_token
180:   arbiter.io.active := active
181:   
182:   // Connect outputs
183:   io.ackA := controllerA.io.ack
184:   io.ackB := controllerB.io.ack
185:   io.ackC := controllerC.io.ack
186:   io.sel := arbiter.io.sel
187:   io.active := active
188:   io.reqA := clientA.io.req
189:   io.reqB := clientB.io.req
190:   io.reqC := clientC.io.req
191:   io.pass_tokenA := controllerA.io.pass_token
192:   io.pass_tokenB := controllerB.io.pass_token
193:   io.pass_tokenC := controllerC.io.pass_token
194: 
195:   // ===== FORMAL ASSERTIONS =====
196: 
197:   // Safety: at most one ack at a time (mutual exclusion)
198:   AssertProperty(!(io.ackA && io.ackB) && !(io.ackA && io.ackC) && !(io.ackB && io.ackC), "ack_mutex")
199: 
200:   // Safety: ack only fires when the corresponding client is requesting
201:   AssertProperty(!io.ackA || io.reqA, "ackA_implies_reqA")
202:   AssertProperty(!io.ackB || io.reqB, "ackB_implies_reqB")
203:   AssertProperty(!io.ackC || io.reqC, "ackC_implies_reqC")
204: 
205:   // Safety: ack only fires when the arbiter has selected that client
206:   AssertProperty(!io.ackA || (io.sel === Selection.A), "ackA_implies_selA")
207:   AssertProperty(!io.ackB || (io.sel === Selection.B), "ackB_implies_selB")
208:   AssertProperty(!io.ackC || (io.sel === Selection.C), "ackC_implies_selC")
209: 
210:   // Bounded liveness: if a client is requesting, it must receive ack within 30 cycles
211:   // The bound is generous: the round-robin cycles through 3 clients, and each
212:   // selected client may hold the arbiter for multiple cycles before releasing.
213:   AssertProperty(io.reqA |-> Sequence(io.ackA).delayRange(1, 30), None, None, Some("reqA_ackA_liveness"))
214:   AssertProperty(io.reqB |-> Sequence(io.ackB).delayRange(1, 30), None, None, Some("reqB_ackB_liveness"))
215:   AssertProperty(io.reqC |-> Sequence(io.ackC).delayRange(1, 30), None, None, Some("reqC_ackC_liveness"))
216: }
217: 
218: // Verilog generator
219: object VerilogGenerator extends App {
220:   emitVerilog(new Main(), args)
221: }

arguments.content:
# Counterexample Analysis Report: `ackA_implies_reqA`

## 1. Verification Environment

- **Top Module**: `Main`
- **Design Under Test**: A round-robin arbiter system with 3 clients (A, B, C) and 3 controllers connected to a shared arbiter
- **Key Components**:
  - `Client` (×3): Generates pseudo-random requests using an LFSR, transitions through states NO_REQ → REQ → HAVE_TOKEN → NO_REQ
  - `Controller` (×3): Acknowledges requests when selected by arbiter, transitions through states IDLE → READY → BUSY → IDLE
  - `Arbiter` (×1): Round-robin selection among clients A→B→C→A
- **Connections**: Each Client's `io.req` drives the corresponding Controller's `io.req`; each Controller's `io.ack` drives the corresponding Client's `io.ack`; the Arbiter's `io.sel` is shared among all Controllers

## 2. Violated Assertion

- **Assertion Name**: `ackA_implies_reqA`
- **Source File**: `arbiter3.scala`, line ~205
- **Code Snippet**:
  ```scala
  AssertProperty(!io.ackA || io.reqA, "ackA_implies_reqA")
  ```
- **Property Description**: The assertion checks that whenever `io_ackA` is asserted (high), `io_reqA` must also be high. In other words, the arbiter should never send an acknowledgement to client A unless client A is actively requesting.

## 3. Waveform Information

- **Waveform File**: `verilog/extra_bench/param_arbiter3/Main.ackA_implies_reqA.fst`
- **Time Range**: 0 ns → 200 ns (20 cycles)
- **Key Time Point**: **T = 190 ns** (cycle 19, positive clock edge)
- **Critical Signal Values at Failure Point (T=190 ns)**:

| Signal | Value |
|--------|-------|
| `Main.io_ackA` | **1** |
| `Main.io_reqA` | **0** ✗ |
| `Main.io_sel [1:0]` | 11 (Selection.X) |
| `Main.io_active` | 0 |
| `Main.controllerA.state [1:0]` | 10 (BUSY) |
| `Main.controllerA.ackReg` | 1 |
| `Main.controllerA.io_req` | 0 |
| `Main.clientA.state [1:0]` | 00 (NO_REQ) |
| `Main.clientA.reqReg` | 0 |
| `Main.clientA.lfsr [7:0]` | 0b10100011 (LSB=1 → randChoice=true) |

## 4. Root Cause Analysis

### Bug Location

- **File**: `arbiter3.scala`, class `Controller`
- **Line**: ~42 (`io.ack := ackReg`)
- **Bug Type**: **Design Bug in the Controller (DUT Bug)**

### Description of the Bug

The **Controller** module drives `io.ack` directly from a registered signal `ackReg`:

```scala
io.ack := ackReg
```

The `ackReg` is set to `true.B` when the Controller enters the READY state and only cleared to `false.B` when the Controller sees `!io.req` in the BUSY state. However, this clearing happens **synchronously** at the next clock edge — there is a one-cycle window where `ackReg` is still high after `io.req` has already dropped.

The proper fix is to gate `io.ack` with `io.req` so that the acknowledgement is withdrawn combinatorially the moment the request drops:

```scala
io.ack := ackReg && io.req
```

### Evidence from the Waveform

The sequence of events leading to the failure at T=190 ns:

1. **T=140–150 ns (cycles 14–15)**: The arbiter sets `io_sel=00` (Selection.A), selecting client A. Controller A is in IDLE state and sees `isSelected=true` and `io_req=1`. It transitions IDLE → READY (state 00→01) at T=150.

2. **T=160 ns (cycle 16)**: Controller A transitions from READY → BUSY (state 01→10) and sets `ackReg=1`. Client A (in REQ state) receives `io_ack=1` and schedules transition to HAVE_TOKEN at T=170. At this point `io_ackA=1` and `io_reqA=1` — assertion holds.

3. **T=170–180 ns (cycles 17–18)**: Client A transitions to HAVE_TOKEN state and holds `reqReg=1`. Controller A remains in BUSY state with `ackReg=1`. Both `io_ackA` and `io_reqA` are 1 — assertion holds.

4. **T=190 ns (cycle 19)**: Client A's LFSR produces `randChoice=true` (bit 0 of 0b10100011 is 1), so the Client transitions from HAVE_TOKEN → NO_REQ and sets `reqReg=0` → `io_reqA=0`. However, Controller A's `ackReg` is still 1 (it will only be cleared at T=200 when the BUSY state sees `!io.req`). This creates a one-cycle mismatch: **`io_ackA=1` while `io_reqA=0`**, violating the assertion.

### Assertion Violation Mechanism

| Cycle | Time | ControllerA.ackReg | ClientA.reqReg | io_ackA | io_reqA | !ackA \|\| reqA |
|-------|------|-------------------|----------------|---------|---------|-----------------|
| 16    | 160  | 1                 | 1              | 1       | 1       | 1 (OK)          |
| 17    | 170  | 1                 | 1              | 1       | 1       | 1 (OK)          |
| 18    | 180  | 1                 | 1              | 1       | 1       | 1 (OK)          |
| **19**| **190**| **1**           | **0**          | **1**   | **0**   | **0 (FAIL)**    |
| 20    | 200  | 0 (cleared)       | 0              | 0       | 0       | 1 (OK)          |

The root cause is a classic **pipeline/mismatch bug**: the Controller does not deassert its acknowledgement combinatorially when the request drops, relying instead on the next clock cycle to clear the ack register. This creates a one-cycle window where a stale acknowledgement exists without a matching request.

### Classification

**Error Type**: `dut_bug` — The Controller's `io.ack` output is not properly gated with `io.req`, causing a stale acknowledgement to persist for one cycle after the request drops.
